rv.q: It’s an imaginative, often engrossing ride.
Nevertheless, the notion of loss and death gives the piece its much needed shadows.
Aside from the underdone setting, Hope has a Happy Meal manages to be both funny and exciting, with well-written and enjoyably performed characters and confident, clear direction.
It's a shame that the promise of political provocation doesn't quite deliver.
I would strongly recommend you buy a ticket and experience it for yourself.
A Happy Meal fails at both, with not much to take away.
I'd highly recommend you taking a trip to the Theatre.

cn.t: Critics find this dystopian satire inventive but uneven, praising strong performances and striking world-building while noting the capitalist critique doesn't fully gel with the family drama at its core.
